statement.p: A vortex that rotates at constant angular velocity w about the z-axis has velocity vector field \vec v = w(-y \vec i + x \vec j).

(a) Sketch, on a separate sheet of paper, the vector field with w = 1 and the vector field with w = -1. Then determine the speed \Vert{\vec v}\Vert of the vortex as a function of the distance from its center, r.
(c) Compute the circulation of \vec v counterclockwise about the circle of radius R in the xy-plane, centered at the origin.

static.solution:
(a) Cross sections of the vector fields are shown below, for w = 1 on the left and for w = -1 on the right. In either case the cross-section is taken in the xy-plane and vectors are drawn with a dot at the tail of each vector.
w = 1 w = -1
The distance from the center of the vortex is given by r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}. The velocity of the vortex at any point is -w y\vec i + w x\vec j, and the speed of the vortex at any point is the magnitude of the velocity, or s=\Vert{\vec {v}}\Vert=\sqrt{(-w y)^2+(w x)^2} =\left|w \right| \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \left| w\right| r.
(b) The divergence of the velocity field is given by: \mbox{div } \vec v = \frac{\partial (-w y)}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial w x}{\partial y} = 0. The curl of the field is: \mbox{curl } \vec{v} = \mbox{curl} (-w y\vec i + w x\vec j) = \left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( w x\right) - \frac{\partial}{\partial y} \left( -w y\right) \right)\vec k = 2w \vec k
(c) We know that \vec{v} has constant magnitude | w | R everywhere on the circle and is everywhere tangential to the circle. In addition, if w > 0, the vector field rotates counterclockwise; if w \lt 0, the vector field rotates clockwise. Thus if w > 0, \vec{v} and d\vec{r} are parallel and in the same direction, so \int_C \vec{v}\cdot d{\vec{r}} = \left| \vec{v}\right| \cdot \left( \mbox{Length of }C \right) = w R\cdot 2\pi R = 2\pi w R^2. If w \lt 0, then \left| w \right| =-w and \vec{v} and d \vec{r} are in opposite directions, so \int_C \vec{v}\cdot {d\vec{r}} = -\left| \vec{v}\right| \cdot \left( \mbox{Length of }C \right) = -\left| w \right| R\cdot \left( 2\pi R\right) = 2\pi w R^2.
